earlier_scan.source_named: Hosokawa, Komei. 1987. 'Malay talk on boat: an account of Broome Pearling Lugger Pidgin' (sketch of the pidgin); not found online.

sources.citation: Hosokawa, Komei. 1994. Retribalization and language mixing: aspects of identity strategies among the Broome Aborigines, Western Australia. Bulletin of the National Museum of Ethnology (Minpaku) 19(3): 491-534. doi:10.15021/00004201
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: About Broome Aboriginal English varieties, not PLP; PLP appears only as a source of loanwords (makan, pikipiki, minom, terrarra, -ka). Its one stress remark (p. 508-509: 'Stress is shown only when it is relevant.. Locative NPs are usually marked by a prominent stress (usually, but not always, on the head noun of the NP)') concerns Yawuru speakers' Aboriginal English, not the pidgin.

sources.citation: Hosokawa, Komei. 1987. Malay talk on boat: an account of Broome Pearling Lugger Pidgin. In Donald C. Laycock & Werner Winter (eds.), A World of Language: Papers presented to Professor S.A. Wurm on his 65th birthday, 287-296. Pacific Linguistics C-100. Canberra: ANU. (open scan of whole volume at ANU Open Research, hdl 1885/145412; image-only, scanned pp. 287-296)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. The sketch is lexical/grammatical/sociohistorical; transcriptions mark vowel length with a colon (po:rr, bure:, kicchi:, banya:, angka:) without comment. Only prosodic remark, p. 292: 'Note that the particle -ka: in (9) is pronounced with a high flat pitch, while it is usually pronounced with a low or mid-high pitch when simply marking a question.' Pp. 292 also note 'phonological modifications peculiar to Japanese' / 'of the kind to Malay' in loanword shapes, segmental only.
No phonology content; used only for its reference list (Hosokawa 1987; McGregor 2004: 69-71; Ethnologue; AUSTLANG P3).
